title: World Champion Gukesh Named to TIME100 Next India Weeks Before First Title Defence
excerpt: The 20-year-old appears in the Phenoms category of TIME's first country-specific Next list, with his profile written by Sharda Ugra.
body:
• World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju, 20, is named in the Phenoms category of TIME100 Next India, TIME's first international edition of its rising-leaders list, released on Thursday.
  • His profile in the list is written by sports journalist Sharda Ugra; the list carries 100 entries across five unranked categories — Artists, Phenoms, Innovators, Leaders and Advocates.
  • Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world chess champion in history in 2024, winning the title at 18.
  • Next up is his first title defence, against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov later this month; the TIME100 Next India gala follows in Mumbai on December 12, with the print issue out December 7.

The reigning world chess champion has been named one of the people shaping India's future by a magazine that has never before built a list like this for a single country. Gukesh Dommaraju appears in the Phenoms category of TIME100 Next India, released on Thursday — the first international edition of TIME's TIME100 Next franchise in the magazine's 103-year history, curated by TIME journalists in India and abroad and presented in partnership with Reliance.

Where he sits in the list

The list divides 100 entries — 102 individuals, counting two duos — into five unranked categories. Gukesh is one of 18 Phenoms, with his profile written by veteran sports journalist Sharda Ugra, according to the full list published by Jagran Josh. He is one of nine athletes honoured across the categories: cricketers Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Harmanpreet Kaur, weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, boxer Lovlina Borgohain, hockey goalkeeper Savita Punia, hurdler Vithya Ramraj, archer Kumkum Mohod and tennis player Sania Mirza, MyKhel reported. Borgohain and Ramraj join him among the Phenoms.

Why India, and why now

TIME announced the India edition on April 23, 2026, at the TIME100 Gala in New York, where TIME chief executive Jessica Sibley and Reliance Foundation chairperson Nita Mukesh Ambani unveiled it onstage. In his November 19 letter to readers, editor-in-chief Sam Jacobs explained the choice of India for the franchise's first country edition with two numbers: hundreds of millions of Indians are under 35, and demographic projections show that by 2030 one in every five working-age people on the planet will be Indian. Jacobs wrote that TIME wanted to capture not only global crossover stars but people whose impact is felt inside Indian communities — a brief that fits a chess champion from Chennai whose following is largest at home.

Why a 20-year-old champion fits a 'next' list

TIME100 Next is a list about trajectory, and Gukesh's is steep by any measure. In December 2024 he defeated Ding Liren to become the youngest undisputed world chess champion in history, at 18 — the first teenager to hold the title. The honour lands in a month that has already underlined the depth behind him: on November 8, Anuj Shrivatri became India's 100th grandmaster, according to KhelNow's records, a milestone no other country's pipeline is currently matching at the top end.

What happens next

The recognition arrives days before the biggest test of Gukesh's career so far. Later this month he defends the world title for the first time, against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov — a challenger from his own generation, which makes the match a meeting of the two players who have defined junior chess's takeover of the elite game. Win, and the TIME listing reads as a coronation; lose, and it becomes a snapshot of how quickly the crown now moves.

TIME's own calendar continues in December: the special print edition reaches newsstands on December 7, and the inaugural TIME100 Next India gala is scheduled for December 12 at Mumbai's Jio World Convention Centre.
